title: Kinematics Module 7 Lesson 2: Sketch Multi Phase Velocity-Time Graph custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line such that its velocity is given by $v(t) = 6t - t^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 3$, and $v(t) = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $3 \le t \le 8$. Find the acceleration of the particle at $t = 2\text{ s}$, and state whether the gradient of the $v$-$t$ graph is continuous at the junction $t = 3\text{ s}$.

The velocity of a particle during a braking phase is modelled by $v(t) = 16 - t^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 4$. State the coordinates of the initial point on the $v$-$t$ graph, and the time at which the particle comes to rest.
For the first stage of motion, $0 \le t \le 6$, a particle's velocity is given by $v(t) = 12t - 2t^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Find the maximum velocity reached and the value of $t$ at which it occurs.

A velocity-time graph consists of a curved phase $v = 3t^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 2$, followed by a constant velocity phase $v = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $2 \le t \le 5$. Calculate the total distance travelled by the particle from $t = 0$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$.

A particle has velocity given by $v(t) = 9t^2 - t^3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 6$. Find the time $t$ at which the acceleration is at a maximum, and state whether the graph of $v$ against $t$ is concave upwards or concave downwards at $t = 1\text{ s}$.

A velocity-time graph has a linear braking stage modelled by $v(t) = 15 - 3t\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $2 \le t \le 8$. Find the time at which the graph crosses the time axis, and find the velocity at $t = 7\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line from rest at $t = 0$. For $0 \le t \le 4$, its velocity is given by $v(t) = 3t^2 - \frac{1}{2}t^3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. For $4 \le t \le 10$, the particle continues to move with constant velocity equal to $v(4)$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the velocity of the particle at $t = 4\text{ s}$, and find its acceleration at $t = 2\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: State the key features needed to sketch the velocity-time graph for $0 \le t \le 10$, including the behavior at $t = 4$, and calculate the total distance travelled by the particle in the $10\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: A particle accelerates from rest with constant acceleration for $0 \le t \le 3$, reaching a velocity of $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 3$. For $3 \le t \le 7$, its velocity is modelled by the quadratic function $v(t) = 12 - \frac{3}{4}(t - 3)^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the constant acceleration during the first stage, and find the velocity of the particle at $t = 7\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total distance travelled by the particle from $t = 0$ to $t = 7\text{ s}$, and state the gradient of the $v$-$t$ graph immediately after $t = 3\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: The velocity of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0 \le t \le 6$, and $v(t) = 63 - 4.5t\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $6 \le t \le 14$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the minimum point of the curve on $0 \le t \le 6$, and find the time at which the particle comes to instantaneous rest during this first stage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Sketch the key features of the velocity-time graph for $0 \le t \le 14$, and calculate the total distance travelled by the particle over the entire $14\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt:
A vehicle moves along a test track with velocity $v(t)\text{ m s}^{-1}$ defined over three intervals:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} 4t & 0 \le t \le 3 \\ 12 + 8(t - 3) - (t - 3)^2 & 3 \le t \le 7 \\ 28 - 7(t - 7) & 7 \le t \le 11 \end{cases}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum velocity reached during the second stage and the time at which it occurs, and determine whether the graph is continuous at $t = 3\text{ s}$ and $t = 7\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total distance travelled by the vehicle from $t = 0$ to $t = 11\text{ s}$, and state whether the graph of $v$ against $t$ has a continuous gradient at $t = 7\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt: The velocity of a particle for $0 \le t \le 6$ is modelled by $v(t) = (t - 2)^2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and for $6 \le t \le 10$ by $v(t) = 16 + 4(t - 6)\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the turning point of the graph for $0 \le t \le 6$, state whether the particle changes its direction of motion at this point, and find the velocity at $t = 6\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that the gradient of the velocity-time graph is continuous at $t = 6\text{ s}$, and calculate the total distance travelled from $t = 0$ to $t = 10\text{ s}$.

questions.prompt:
A high-speed train moves along a straight track between two stations, starting from rest at $t = 0$ and coming to rest at $t = 35\text{ s}$. Its velocity $v(t)\text{ m s}^{-1}$ is given by:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} 0.8t^2 & 0 \le t \le 5 \\ 2t + 10 & 5 \le t \le 15 \\ 49 - 0.04t^2 & 15 \le t \le 35 \end{cases}$$

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Verify the continuity of velocity at the two transition times $t = 5\text{ s}$ and $t = 15\text{ s}$, and determine the velocity of the train at $t = 35\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Analyse the gradient and curvature across all three stages, and find the total distance between the two stations.

questions.prompt:
The velocity of a car during a brake test is modelled by:
$$v(t) = \begin{cases} 24 + 6t - \frac{3}{4}t^2 & 0 \le t \le 4 \\ 36 - 3(t - 4) & 4 \le t \le 16 \end{cases}$$
where $t$ is the time in seconds from the beginning of the test.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum velocity reached during the test, verify that the velocity and its gradient are both continuous at $t = 4\text{ s}$, and find the time at which the car comes to rest.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total distance travelled by the car from $t = 0$ to $t = 16\text{ s}$, and find the average speed of the car over this duration.
